subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: Which context-overflow facts should OpenClaw show to end users versus keep only in logs or metadata?
rationale: The code already has token, model, route, and session facts, but exposing raw session keys/channel identifiers and exact token counts changes user-facing privacy and support behavior that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Show redacted diagnostics
options.body: Expose provider/model, effective context budget, observed or estimated token count, overage, and a redacted channel/session label while keeping raw identifiers in logs.

options.title: Keep specifics operator-only
options.body: Leave chat copy generic and document how operators can inspect logs or status metadata for detailed context-pressure facts.

options.title: Defer to broader visibility design
options.body: Keep this narrow issue open but wait for a broader context-visibility plan to decide UI, logs, and channel-message behavior together.

recommendation.title: Show redacted diagnostics
recommendation.body: Expose provider/model, effective context budget, observed or estimated token count, overage, and a redacted channel/session label while keeping raw identifiers in logs.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent routing signal across the visible overflow recovery and auto-reply surfaces plus prior review context on the issue.
